'''''Agave macroacantha''''', the '''black-spined agave''' or '''large-thorned agave''', is a species of succulent [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Asparagaceae]] naturally occurring in [[Oaxaca]] and also near the town of [[Tehuacán, Puebla|Tehuacan]] in the State of [[Puebla]], Mexico.<ref>Zuccarini, Joseph Gerhard. Nova Acta Physico-medica Academiae Caesareae Leopoldino-Carolinae Naturae Curiosorum Exhibentia Ephemerides sive Observationes Historias et Experimenta 16(2): 676. 1833.</ref>

==Description==
''Agave macroacantha'' produces a medium-sized leaf [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]] that can be basal or can grow on a very short stem. Leaves are [[succulent]], greyish green and up to 1.8 feet long at a maximum, ending in sharp black spines that are up to 1.2 inches long at the tips. Flowers are small, grey and red, growing in bunches on sturdy stems of up to 3 m (10 feet) in height.<ref>Gentry, Howard Scott. Agaves of Continental North America. University of Arizona Press, Tucson, 1992.</ref>

==Cultivation==
The plant prefers a dry, sunny and hot location for summer and from early autumn onwards a cooler, well-lit space. It likes regular watering in summer and only minimum watering in winter, and will fare well in a large pot with sparse, gravelly soil.<ref>[http://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=2797 San Marcos Growers, Agave macroacantha]</ref><ref name="sdfkljsadfhso">[http://www.cactus-art.biz/schede/AGAVE/Agave_macroacantha/Agave_macroacantha_viridis/Agave_macracantha_viridis.htm Cactus Art Nursery, Agave macroacantha viridis]</ref><ref>[http://www.cycadpalm.com/agmapl.html Jurassic Garden.com:  ''Agave macroacantha''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150928061824/http://www.cycadpalm.com/agmapl.html |date=2015-09-28 }}, image.</ref>
